reviews.author: idea-repo
reviews.body:
Review from idea-repo (positioning against the Brief, rev 4, and prior_work.md). The experimental content matches the pre-registered definitions (H1-H4, closure vs LOBO with censored k*, grid-averaged paired gap, two-predictor headline k* with the low-bias caveat, three-tier theory check, honest negative H1/H4 outcomes, small-N panels, union overlap). Two positioning points should change before approval; the rest is optional.

Required
1. Scope in the abstract and introduction. The abstract opens "Running a new language model on every benchmark..." and the title/intro speak of "a new model"/"a language model", but the evidence is MTEB embedding models plus the 57 subjects of one benchmark (HELM MMLU); the Brief says "no claim about generative LLMs rests on MTEB alone". The limitation is stated only in Discussion (2). Please put one sentence in the abstract and one in the Introduction naming the data: "embedding-model results (MTEB) and the 57 subjects of one benchmark (HELM MMLU); we do not test suites of benchmarks for generative language models, where our dense blocks have N<12", and frame the first sentence as motivation, not as the scope of the results.
2. Novelty wording in Related work. "None treats the choice of the k runs as a design problem" is an absolute claim from a search that cannot be exhaustive. Write "Among the work we read, none ..." (same for "Neighbouring work answers other questions" if it implies completeness).

Optional
3. Abstract: "greedy Bayesian A-optimal selection (it minimises the average posterior variance...)" - greedy selection reduces it step by step; say "greedily minimises" or "chooses benchmarks one at a time to reduce".
4. Cite the sources of the selector baselines where they are named in Method (pivoted QR / leverage scores: mahoney2009cur is already in the bib; k-medoids and D-optimal need no new entry if described as defined here).
5. Related work could add one clause that adaptive selection (choose the next benchmark after seeing the last score) is the analogue of adaptive testing; the paper tests it (Appendix Table adaptive) and cites fluid2025 only for items.

No change needed to the claims on contribution order, the H2/H4 outcomes or the matrix-Chernoff statement (matches theory_sources.md; the with-replacement/without-replacement caveat is stated).

reviews.author: internal-review-repo
reviews.body:
Request changes on `final` (main head 13c249e, document built-from 13c249e). Full record: internal-review-repo `reviews/paper-repo-7-final-13c249e.md`.

What I checked and found supported: the headline numbers (closure, k* with CIs/censoring, greedy-vs-random gaps, paired shift comparisons, theory gaps) all match `results/*.csv`; deviations are reported as they fell; negative results (H1, H2 margin, H4, coherence, vacuous Chernoff) are stated.

**must M1 — the setting with missing cells is never evaluated.** The objective's setting is a leaderboard matrix with missing cells and a new model with k measured entries. Every result is on dense blocks cut from the leaderboard (124 of 535 models x 70 of 567 tasks; 117 x 247 of 535 x 1256) which, by Table 1, differ systematically from the rest (outside models larger, newer, 0.7-0.9 SD higher). A masked-EM factor model exists in `code/bmk/fa.py` but is not run on a sparse matrix; the history sweep masks cells of the history only, test models stay complete. Narrowing the claim to "the pool" is honest but does not answer whether greedy selection + factor model works on the matrix as it is.
Answer with: the grouped protocol on the full sparse MTEB matrix, or graded-density subsets (coverage e.g. >=30/50/70%), factor model by masked EM, candidate set = benchmarks observed for the test model, targets = random 30% of its observed cells; greedy A vs random vs column mean, k-curve with family-clustered intervals, and a stated LOBO analogue for closure. A main-text paragraph/figure plus an appendix table suffices; the dense-pool results stay as the controlled experiment. Owners: experiment-repo (run), figtab-repo (figure/table), paper-repo (text).

may: (m1) abstract: say the pre-specified 10% margin of H2 is met on one pool of three; (m2) checklist: "seven limitations" vs six in Section 7, "5-20 CPU minutes" vs 2-22 in Appendix D; (m3) define "closure" and "A-optimal" in a clause in the abstract; (m4) say where the pre-specification is recorded (Brief revision/commit).
